scope.population: late-half fills of the 2,069 wallets that clear the 50-fill early-half floor, 852,035 fills, which is 69.0 per cent of the 1,234,777 late-half fills: a wallet under the floor carries no label and its fills belong to no decile, so this is NOT the late half. Cut into ten groups of equal WALLET count and therefore unequal fill count, a factor of 19 between the largest and the smallest; the tenth decile holds 206 wallets and 56.2 per cent of the fills. The baseline block of the same artifact measures every late fill and is therefore a wider population than this one
scope.window: single December window; days 4-8 label the wallets and the disjoint days 9-13 carry every net figure drawn

declared_not_confirmed.note: settings.py declares these; this run did not state what it used, so they are the declaration and not a property of this artifact

settings_fingerprint.overrides_note: this file draws and computes no new quantity: every net figure is read from maker_econ_results.json, and the only things computed here are two rank correlations, a gap and a share, all of them deterministic functions of the numbers read. No random stream is drawn, so no seed, no permutation count and no bootstrap count apply and each is stated as not applying rather than left to be read as the declaration. The fill floor, the horizon and the reference price are read from settings.py at run time and are never typed here

question: does what is known about a counterparty BEFORE a fill order the maker's net result AFTER it, on fills the ranking never saw

summary.interpretation: the two weightings answer two questions and disagree on purpose. Per fill the ordering is almost perfect, so the pre-trade rank sorts the typical fill. By notional the first nine deciles sit in a band and the tenth drops away by -2.48 bps, and that tenth carries 56.2 per cent of the late fills, so the loss is concentrated where the volume already was rather than spread along the ranking

population_is_narrower_than_the_late_hal.note: a wallet under the 50-fill early floor carries no label, so its late fills belong to no decile. The ten cells hold 69.0 per cent of the late half and the caption says so. The floor buys reliability of the ranking and costs coverage, and the two move against each other across the rungs recorded in all_slices

fills_per_decile_are_not_equal.note: the deciles are equal in WALLETS and unequal in FILLS by a factor of 19 here, so bars of equal width would invite a reader to weigh ten cells that do not carry equal weight. The lower strip of the figure carries the share of every decile, each one labelled, rather than encoding it in the width of the bar above, because a width that varies with the count makes the AREA of a bar meaningless while its height is the quantity

sign_depends_on_reference_price_and_fee.note: the sign of a decile is a property of the reference price and the fee rung and not of the ranking, so the caption names all three. The drawn cell has no positive decile; other cells of the same rung do. The panel never mixes two reference prices on one axis

what_the_measure_is_not: net_MID_lower is half the quoted spread minus the mid markout minus the maker fee. The half-spread is the quoted one, so the measure is a lower bound on the SPREAD INCOME a maker realises; it is not a lower bound on profit, because the exit and the funding on the inventory the fills leave behind are outside the model. The figure is read across the ranking and not at the level of one bar
no_uncertainty_here: the decile table of maker_econ_results.json carries no bootstrap interval on any cell; the interval machinery of that file is attached to the policy block instead. Nothing is drawn as an error bar and no cell is claimed individually. The first decile holds 2.9 per cent of the late fills, so its notional-weighted figure rests on few large prints and is not commented on

out_of_sample_premise.checked_here: the two day sets are read from the source artifact and their intersection is asserted empty before anything is drawn; the producer asserts the same at the fill level
out_of_sample_premise.qualification: the pre-trade rank is itself built from realised outcomes of EARLIER fills, which is the mechanism under test rather than a leak of it: no fill on the vertical axis contributed to the horizontal one

decile_is_not_the_toxic_cut.note: the tenth decile and the toxic cut used by the policy block are built by two different roundings of the same top ten per cent and differ by one wallet, so the caption says decile and not toxic cut

robustness_across_slices.note: eight fill-floor rungs against two horizons. The companion horizon is 60 seconds, the companion reference price is net_PRINT and the companion fee tier is t4_0fee; all of them are in the sweep below and none is drawn
